details:
It is a necessary decision to take full advantage of VRC's keen community developer and creator user base.
Adding an Experimental branch will give helpful insight and form refined plans for what to invest time into producing. Content from this branch may take years to reach the public or maybe not see a full release, but VRC will still get informed feedback. Content can be feature complete, release ready, or bug fixes but just there to tinker with, similar to a preview.
Who is this for:
- Community Developers and Creators, the heart of the community pumping creations into VRC and consistently giving fresh content to the platform.
Why:
- Existing services like Unreal Engine, Blender, and other software platforms already have "experimental" and preview releases as entire sections for features that are in limbo and may never come but letting developers tinker with them. 
- It would allow developers to create content without having to be released to the public branch or worrying about having to support it long-term.
- Not all experiments leave a preview, and some stay indefinitely, but they were excellent learning experiences for both platform holders and content creators.
- This is before even Alphas and Betas, basically "non-Production." 
- Dev Jams results can reach the experimental branch and get outside input without waiting for features to be pushed into production for feedback.
How:
- Add a separate permanent branch that doesn't mix with betas or public release
- It can have its exclusive world lists only accessible from its branch
- SDKs updated with package toggles and versioning from the new Creator Companion 
- Streamers and content creators going over to the experimental branch is suitable for driving player interest in features.
title: Lab Rats: Experimental Feature Branch
